question: Should OpenClaw add a core startup-loaded immutable operator policy overlay that outranks mutable config and rejects weakening writes, or should immutable baseline handling remain in Policy/Nix-style conformance surfaces?
rationale: The choice changes config precedence, runtime security guarantees, status/doctor diagnostics, and compatibility expectations; current main only has adjacent conformance checks and install-mode immutability.

options.title: Implement core immutable overlay
options.body: Define a startup-loaded operator policy source with locked precedence, config-write conflict checks, status/doctor visibility, focused tests, and public docs.

options.title: Keep conformance-only policy
options.body: Document that operators should use Policy, policy compare, attestations, and Nix-managed config for audits while runtime config remains the mutable source of truth.

options.title: Defer until hooks settle
options.body: Leave the issue open while related policy-hook proposals clarify whether enforcement belongs in plugin hooks, core config/write paths, or both.

recommendation.title: Implement core immutable overlay
recommendation.body: Define a startup-loaded operator policy source with locked precedence, config-write conflict checks, status/doctor visibility, focused tests, and public docs.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc owns the issue and authored the prior exact implementation candidate, making them the clearest decision owner for the security-boundary direction.
